back: Outcomes: what must be true (behavior, tests, docs). Constraints: what must not happen (off-limit files, no new deps, budgets).
CI/test pass rate, coverage or test-count change, scan findings (CodeQL, lint), diff size vs scope, review iterations, time to merge, revert rate, cost.
Reviewer judgment of correctness/clarity, adherence to conventions, PR description quality, trust to merge.

front: What does 'align evaluation with development intent' protect against?
back: Gaming metrics, e.g. deleting a failing test or swallowing exceptions so checks go green without solving the real problem.
CodeQL, Advisory Database check for new dependencies, secret scanning, plus Copilot code review. No GHAS license required.

front: Where do you inspect what an agent did and saw?
back: Session logs (also plans, tool-call traces, outputs, PR timeline, workflow artifacts).
Reasoning errors, tool misuse, context/environment issues.
Misreading the requirement, scope creep, ignoring a stated constraint, wrong plan.
Wrong arguments, wrong tool, repeating a failing call, denied tool, MCP server not started.
Missing dependency, firewall block, stale/conflicting instructions or memory, flaky test.

front: Triage questions for a failed run?
back: Did it understand the task? Did it call the right tools correctly? Did the environment allow success?
Sharper acceptance criteria, plan validation, smaller tasks, examples.
Correct tool config/allowlist, instructions on tool usage, remove unneeded tools.
copilot-setup-steps, firewall allowlist, prune or fix stale context, stabilize flaky tests.
Instructions, workflows, constraints, memory usage, tool usage/access.
Evaluation set > baseline > classify failures > change ONE lever > re-run same set > compare > keep/revert.

front: Why change one variable at a time?
back: So you can attribute the improvement or regression to a specific change.
Tuning from one anecdote, changing many things at once, loosening permissions as a fix, adding instructions for an environment fault.

front: How should instructions be written for tuning?
back: Specific, testable, non-contradictory, with an explicit verification step (for example run tests before finishing).

front: Best way to compare plan vs result during analysis?
back: Line up the plan, tool-call trace and final diff; find the first divergence.
